summary: Piotr Klafkowski (1953–2002) was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski, and also studied under Lozang Jamspal, Geleg Gyatso, and Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé (1897–1970) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Palzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and later taught Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka (1884–1964) worked in linguistics, Indology, and archaeology. After studying under Nicolaas Johannes Krom at Leiden University, he served at the National Museum of Indonesia and held professorships at Gadjah Mada University, University of Indonesia, and Udayana University.

Polly Young-Eisendrath (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies and related fields. She earned an MA at Goddard College, a PhD at Washington University in St. Louis, and trained with Philip Kapleau, later serving as clinical associate professor at the University of Vermont.
Pori Park specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and has served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held positions at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and served as Professor at the University of Calcutta, where he was attested in 2009.
Prabhasa Dharma Cheney (1931–1999) was active in Buddhist and religious studies. She undertook traditional training under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki beginning in 1967 and also studied under Seikō Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1898–1956) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. Educated at the University of Calcutta and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, he held posts at the University of Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.

Pradyot Kumar Mukhopadhyay (born 1938) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Jadavpur University and was a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 2009).

Prafulla Chandra Ray (1861–1944) was a scholar in history and other fields. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and University of Edinburgh, holding posts at Presidency College, the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture, and the University of Calcutta.

Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Patna University and Visva-Bharati University. He served as a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati, Professor at Utkal University (~1953–1974), and Principal at Gangadhar Meher University (~1967–1968).

Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) was an art historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Mumbai. He worked at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya and held professorships at the University of Chicago and Harvard University (1980–2004).
Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and completed his PhD at the University of Mysore, attested in 2014.

Pratap Chandra Chunder (1919–2008) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, where he studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.
Pratap Kumar Penumala is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. In 2010, he was attested as a Professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a Visiting Professor at Colorado College.

Pratapaditya Pal (born 1935) specializes in history, Indology, and Tibetology, having earned PhDs from Calcutta and Cambridge. He was a curator at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and held multiple curatorial and directorial roles at LACMA (~1970–1995).

Prayudh Payutto (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He graduated from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he served as Associate Dean (~1964–1972), and was appointed Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.

id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark (1908–1980) was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the London School of Economics (~1935–1939) and worked at the Office of Strategic Services (~1944–1945).

Prods Oktor Skjærvø (born 1944) specializes in Iranian linguistics. Educated at Oslo and Mainz, he held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Columbia University as an editor for Encyclopædia Iranica, and Harvard University as Aga Khan Professor of Iranian Studies (~1991–2015).

Pulinbihari Chakravarti was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society, attested in 1951.
